finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns any invoice record to any caller who knows its ID. There is no ownership check (inv['customer'] vs g.user['id']) and no login guard on the route, unlike the sibling /my/invoice/<inv_id> route. This is an insecure direct object reference (broken object-level authorization).
finding.source: inv_id path parameter (invoices.py:7-8), attacker-controlled, and the caller's identity is never consulted.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returning the full invoice record (invoices.py:10), including the customer field.

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator or before_request in this file.
inv_id taken directly from the URL.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) lookup; no comparison of the record's owner to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: No login_required or equivalent decorator on the route. No g.user reference in this handler. No customer/tenant comparison before jsonify. Sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> at lines 16-17 does perform the owner check, so the omission here is specific to this route. Upstream middleware is not present in the repo; if a global before_request enforces login, the flaw still stands as authenticated IDOR (any logged-in user reads any invoice). If no global auth exists, it is unauthenticated. Exploitability depends on how invoice IDs are generated: sequential or guessable IDs make it trivial, while unguessable UUIDs require an ID leak elsewhere.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7 has no auth decorator, invoices.py:8-10 has no ownership comparison before jsonify, and the repo contains no before_request or login_required (grep finds only the four route lines and g.user at invoices.py:16 and 23). The sibling check at invoices.py:16-17 is not applied to this route.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches invoices.py:7-10, and get_invoice returns INVOICES[inv_id] at invoices.py:9-10 with no owner check, while get_my_invoice enforces inv["customer"] == g.user["id"] at invoices.py:16-17. Any caller who knows an ID can read it, so the finding holds whether or not a global auth layer exists outside this file, and exploitability depends on ID guessability as the candidate notes. The trace's "no login guard, unlike the sibling" wording is slightly off because the sibling also has no login decorator and only relies on g.user, but that does not change the IDOR.
